wa_guye_peak_improbable_traverse.notes: Initial low to mid-5th class climbing through loose, crumbly rhyolite terrain; lots of holds but quality poor and exposed
Continuation of crumbly terrain leading toward Lunch Ledge; climbers should carefully test all holds
Final approach to Lunch Ledge (~300 ft from start); large comfortable belay ledge provides good rest point before upper pitches

The iconic Improbable Traverse pitch(es): traverse right on good foot ledges with several old fixed pitons for protection. Critical: November 2021 rockfall destroyed ~30x40ft section; now requires downclimbing 5.9-5.10 from old pin with 30+ feet of unprotected traversing. Many now recommend this route is not safe.
Class 4 ramp climbing through alpine trees and rock slabs to summit ridge approach; short but exposed

wa_leche_la_vaca.notes: Fun chimney far right on the wall past a small tree onto a knobby slab; a spicy 5.8 move left leads to another knobby slab and a corner belay.
Fun corner up to a flake; move left around the flake (5.9 crux move) into a knob-footed corner to a ledge.
A large, left-leaning 5.10 layback corner — a #4 Camalot eases the run-out feel — continuing to a big belay ledge.
Beautiful knobby white rock to a small roof; a 5.10 move surmounts the roof, then crack and knobs lead to a ledge belay.
Move up and left on 4th-class ground traversing toward the summit, steepening to low fifth near the end; about 100 m to the summit block, commonly simul-climbed.
